newsitem.title: NORWAY: Saga sells Indonesian oil block stake.
newsitem.headline: Saga sells Indonesian oil block stake.

text.p: Saga Petroleum ASA said on Monday it had signed an agreement to sell its 50 percent stake in the Jambi Merang oil prospect in Indonesia to New Zealand's Cue Energy Resources.
The agreed sale price for the block is 191 million crowns, effective from January 1, 1997, Saga said in a statement to the Oslo bourse.
Norway's largest listed oil company said it is also in the last stages of negotiations with another company to sell its 30 percent interest in the North West Nautana Sea block II.
The company said the book value of its activities in Indonesia was 98 million crowns at the end of 1996.

"Saga has decided to pull out from Indonesia at the end of 1996 in order to focus the company's international activities in Northwest Europe (UK, Ireland and the Faroe Islands) and in Libya as well as southwest Africa," the statement said.
The sale of the Nautuna Sea block will terminate Saga's activities in the area.
